question: What is the main fluid that the lymphatic system collects from our body tissues?

options.A: Interstitial fluid that leaked from blood capillaries
options.B: Pure water absorbed directly from the digestive tract
options.C: Intracellular fluid released from damaged muscle cells
options.D: Cerebrospinal fluid produced within brain ventricles

explanation: Think of the lymphatic system as the body's cleaning crew! It picks up the extra fluid (interstitial fluid) that constantly leaks out of our tiny blood vessels into our tissues, returning it safely to circulation. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T13#GNS111_U2_T13_h1)

question: Why does lymph fluid need our skeletal muscles to move around the body?

options.A: The system lacks a central muscular pump like the heart
options.B: Skeletal muscles actively produce all circulating white blood cells
options.C: Muscle movement heats up the lymph to speed up filtration
options.D: Contractions prevent red blood cells from entering lymph vessels

explanation: Unlike blood, which is pumped everywhere by the heart, lymph doesn't have its own pump. It relies on us moving our muscles and breathing to squeeze it along! [learn more](GNS111_U2_T13#GNS111_U2_T13_h1)

question: Where do the main lymphatic ducts finally empty their fluid contents?

options.A: Into the large subclavian veins near the heart
options.B: Back through the walls of the small intestines
options.C: Directly into the chambers of the right atrium
options.D: Into the peritoneal cavity for local absorption

explanation: After cleaning up and traveling through the vessels, lymph is finally emptied back into the big subclavian veins right near the heart to rejoin the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T13#GNS111_U2_T13_h2)

question: What is the main job of the tiny valves inside collecting lymphatic vessels?

options.A: To speed up the heart rate during physical exertion
options.B: To mix red blood cells into the lymphatic fluid
options.C: To filter out bacteria before reaching the lymph nodes
options.D: To prevent the backward flow of lymph against gravity

explanation: Just like one-way doors, these valves make sure that as muscle movement pushes lymph upward, it can't slip back down. It's all about moving forward! [learn more](GNS111_U2_T13#GNS111_U2_T13_h2)

question: Through which vessels does lymph flow as it enters a lymph node?
explanation: A easy trick to remember: 'A'fferent 'A'rrives (brings lymph into the node), while 'E'fferent 'E'xits (carries filtered lymph away). You've got this! [learn more](GNS111_U2_T13#GNS111_U2_T13_h3)

question: Why does lymph slow down as it passes through a lymph node?

options.A: To allow excess water to evaporate through the skin surface
options.B: To let red blood cells mix thoroughly with the lymph
options.C: To cool down the fluid before it enters the bloodstream
options.D: To give immune cells enough time to detect and fight pathogens

explanation: Slowing down the traffic inside the lymph node gives the immune cells (our body's security guards) enough time to check the fluid for germs and start fighting back if needed. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T13#GNS111_U2_T13_h3)

question: Which organ is mainly responsible for filtering blood and recycling old red blood cells?
explanation: The spleen is like a master recycler and blood filter. It catches old, worn-out red blood cells and also helps store platelets and fight infections. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T13#GNS111_U2_T13_h4)

question: What is the main job of the thymus gland during a person's early development?

options.A: Secretion of digestive enzymes into the stomach
options.B: Production of red blood cells for fetal circulation
options.C: Maturation of T-lymphocytes for adaptive immunity
options.D: Filtration of excess fluid from tissue spaces

explanation: Think of the thymus as a special training school for white blood cells! Immature T-cells go there to graduate and learn how to defend the body against invaders. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T13#GNS111_U2_T13_h4)

question: A patient who had a left-sided mastectomy (breast removal surgery) is on your ward. What important precaution should you take?

options.A: Avoid taking blood pressure measurements on the left arm
options.B: Administer all intravenous medications into the left forearm
options.C: Encourage heavy weightlifting exercises with the left arm
options.D: Apply tight compression bandages constantly to both arms

explanation: When lymph nodes are removed during surgery, fluid drainage in that arm is compromised. Putting pressure on it with a BP cuff can easily trigger severe swelling (lymphedema) and infection. Always protect the affected arm! [learn more](GNS111_U2_T13#GNS111_U2_T13_h5)

question: What does a clinical finding of hard, fixed, and painless (non-tender) lymph nodes usually suggest?
explanation: As a general clinical rule: soft, tender, and movable nodes usually point to an infection or inflammation. On the other hand, hard, fixed nodes that don't hurt often raise suspicion for cancer and need further investigation. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T13#GNS111_U2_T13_h5)
